rationale.conceptual: Standard density functional theory (DFT) with widely used van der Waals correction and hybrid functional; the analysis of band alignment types and water splitting feasibility is routine in this subfield. No custom method or novel algorithm is required.
rationale.execution: The workflow consists of ~5 stages (monolayer relax, heterostructure construction/relax, AIMD, electronic structure with PBE and HSE06, photocatalytic evaluation) with dependencies between steps. Setting up the DFT environment and managing multiple calculations and output parsing is moderately complex.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard DFT protocols (PBE+D2, HSE06) to well-known 2D materials, requiring no novel theory, so conceptual difficulty is low. The reproduction pipeline involves multiple steps (monolayer relax, heterobilayer stacking, AIMD, band structure, alignment classification) that demand careful orchestration but remain within typical computational chemistry workflows.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small heterostructure cells (few atoms per unit cell) with moderate k-point sampling and a hybrid functional; calculations can run on a single multi-core CPU node with ~16 GB RAM; no large data dependencies.
